text.p: Tadiran Telecommunications Ltd's first-quarter results reflect a shift in its sales focus from Bezeq Israel Telecom to exports, company officials said on Monday.

"Although our revenues increased only modestly this quarter, they reflect our fundamental shift from a domestic to an export-oriented organisation. This is a profound change in our business which required adjustments in our marketing strategy, product development efforts, business organisation and business model," said president and chief executive Haim Rosen.

While first-quarter sales for the Israeli maker of telecom equipment rose to $116.9 million from $114.4 million a year earlier, net income dropped to $5.1 million, or $0.20 a share, from $12 million, or $0.60 a share.
Net research and development expenses grew to $10.4 million from $8.2 million while selling and marketing expenses jumped to $11.3 million from $7.6 million.
The company said it was the first quarter in which marketing expenses outpaced R&D spending.
Sales to state-controlled Bezeq declined in the quarter to $30 from $56 million a year earlier while exports grew to $63 from $36 million.
Exports for all of 1996 rose by nearly 50 percent to $174 million from $119 million in 1995.
Equity analysts predict exports will continue to grow by about 50 percent in 1997.
As Tadiran, a subsidiary of Tadiran Ltd, becomes less dependent on local sales "it will be a better and more balanced company," said Tadiran Telecom chairman Israel Zamir.
At a news conference he said total sales in 1997 will be at least at the same level as in 1996.
Despite the need for increased investment in marketing and R&D, analysts expect the negative impact on earnings in 1997 to be offset by higher margins and increased dollar volume.
Gross margins for the products sold overseas are better than for products sold locally, chief financial officer Haim Fishler said.
Internationally the company focuses on providing digital cross connect systems and wireless local loop systems.
Last year represented a record year for Tadiran in terms of sales to Bezeq as the state phone company completed the digitalisation of its network.

Most of this process was finished by the third quarter of 1996. Rosen said it was therefore more appropriate to compare the first quarter of 1997 with the fourth quarter of 1996, which already reflected a decline in sales to Bezeq.
By the fourth quarter of 1996 exports accounted for more than 50 percent of Tadiran's sales. Total sales in the fourth quarter were $102.1 million while net profit was $3.7 million.
To gain technology and know-how Tadiran intends to acquire small companies while it seeks strategic alliances to market its products overseas.
Tadiran's orders backlog at the end of the first quarter totalled $140 million, up by about $10 million from the end of 1996.
